record.original_question: A strong edge coloring of a graph assigns colors to edges so that any two edges that are adjacent or both adjacent to a common edge receive distinct colors; equivalently, it is a proper vertex-coloring of the square of the line graph. If a diamond-free claw-free cubic graph is obtained by truncating a cubic graph G, denoted T(G), is every such graph strongly 6-edge-colorable? Equivalently, is χ′_s(T(G)) = 6 for every cubic graph G?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a simple graph. A strong edge coloring of G is an assignment of colors to the edges of G such that any two edges that are either adjacent (share an endpoint) or both adjacent to a common third edge receive distinct colors; equivalently, it is a proper vertex coloring of the square of the line graph of G. The strong chromatic index χ′_s(G) is the minimum number of colors in such a coloring.

A graph is claw-free if it contains no induced K_{1,3}, and diamond-free if it contains no induced K_4 minus an edge. A graph is cubic if every vertex has degree 3.

The truncation T(G) of a cubic graph G is the cubic graph obtained from G by replacing each vertex v of G with a triangle, where the three edges of G incident to v are attached, one each, to the three distinct vertices of the corresponding triangle. The resulting graph T(G) is cubic, claw-free, and diamond-free, and conversely every connected diamond-free claw-free cubic graph (other than K_4) arises as T(G) for some cubic multigraph G.

For every cubic (multi)graph G, the graph T(G) satisfies χ′_s(T(G)) ≥ 6. Prove or disprove: for every cubic graph G one has χ′_s(T(G)) = 6; equivalently, every diamond-free claw-free cubic graph is strongly 6-edge-colorable.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question at the 33rd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings (2024). Related results give upper bounds of 7 for strong chromatic index of claw-free subcubic graphs (Lv, Li, Zhu and others), but the specific equality χ′_s(T(G)) = 6 for all cubic G does not appear to be resolved in the recent literature.

status_evidence.title: The Tight Bound for the Strong Chromatic Indices of Claw-Free Subcubic Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: A claw-free subcubic graph other than the triangular prism has strong chromatic index at most 7.
status_evidence.claim: Best known general upper bound for claw-free subcubic graphs is 7, not 6, suggesting the 6-bound for truncations of cubic graphs remains open.

status_evidence.title: A note on strong edge-coloring of claw-free cubic graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Strong edge-coloring of claw-free cubic graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to study strong edge colorings of claw-free cubic graphs without resolving the truncation conjecture χ′_s(T(G))=6.
